heading: LESSON OBJECTIVE
text: Translate points and polygons on a coordinate plane using a given horizontal and vertical shift, and find a missing shift from an original point and its image.

heading: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
text: A translation slides every point the same distance in the same direction without turning or flipping the shape. It preserves side lengths, angles, orientation, area, and perimeter.

heading: KEY DEFINITIONS
text: Preimage: original figure. Image: moved figure, often marked with a prime such as A′. Translation vector (a,b): horizontal change a and vertical change b. Right and up are positive; left and down are negative.

heading: CORE RULE
text: Under translation T(x,y)=(x+a,y+b), add a to every x-coordinate and b to every y-coordinate. The shift from P(x,y) to P′(x′,y′) is (x′−x,y′−y).

heading: HOW IT WORKS
text: Read the translation vector. Move right for positive a or left for negative a; move up for positive b or down for negative b. Apply the same ordered pair to every vertex, then connect corresponding image vertices in the original order.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — NEGATIVE SHIFT
text: Translate Q(−4,5) five units left and two units down. Vector=(−5,−2). Q′=(−9,3).

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — TRIANGLE
text: Translate A(1,1), B(3,1), C(2,4) by (3,−2). The image vertices are A′(4,−1), B′(6,−1), C′(5,2). Every vertex moves right 3 and down 2.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — FIND THE VECTOR
text: If M(−2,4) maps to M′(3,−1), then horizontal change=3−(−2)=5 and vertical change=−1−4=−5. The translation vector is (5,−5).

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — MISSING PREIMAGE
text: If a translation by (−3,6) sends R to R′(1,2), undo the shift: R=(1−(−3),2−6)=(4,−4).

heading: DETERMINISTIC GRAPH STRATEGY
text: Plot the triangle A(1,1), B(3,1), C(2,4) and its image A′(4,−1), B′(6,−1), C′(5,2). The verified displacement of each corresponding vertex is (3,−2). Connect vertices in matching order; do not approximate coordinates from a decorative image.

heading: COMMON MISTAKES
text: Do not swap horizontal and vertical changes. A negative horizontal shift moves left, not down. Do not change the sign twice when undoing a translation. Do not apply different vectors to different vertices.

heading: EXAM STRATEGY
text: Subtract corresponding coordinates to find the vector. For a missing image, add the vector; for a missing preimage, subtract it. Check one more vertex to verify the same shift was used throughout.

heading: QUICK CHECK
text: (1,2) shifted by (4,−3) becomes (5,−1). (−3,5) shifted left 2 becomes (−5,5). The vector from (2,−1) to (−1,4) is (−3,5).

heading: LESSON RECAP
text: Translation means add one constant to all x-values and another to all y-values: (x,y)→(x+a,y+b). The vector between corresponding points is (Δx,Δy). Shape and orientation are preserved.
